entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen29778" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen29779" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen29780" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen29780" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen29779" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen29781" type="x-p"/> By the significant type of breaking a potter's vessel, Jeremiah is directed to predict the utter desolation of Judah and Jerusalem, <reference osisRef="Jer.19.1-Jer.19.15">Jer 19:1-15</reference>. The prophets taught frequently by symbolic actions as well as by words. <div eID="gen29781" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29782" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen29782" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29783" type="x-p"/> Go and get a potter's earthen bottle - This discourse was also delivered some time in the reign of Jehoiakim. Under the type of breaking a potter's earthen bottle or jug, Jeremiah shows his enemies that the word of the Lord should stand, that Jerusalem should be taken and sacked, and they all carried into captivity. <div eID="gen29783" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29784" type="x-p"/> Ancients of the priests - The chiefs of the twenty-four classes which David had established. See <reference osisRef="1Chr.24.4">1Chr 24:4</reference>.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen29786" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29787" type="x-p"/> I will make void the counsel of Judah - Probably this refers to some determination made to proclaim themselves independent, and pay no more tribute to the Chaldeans. <div eID="gen29787" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29788" type="x-p"/> To be meat for the fowls - See on <reference osisRef="Jer.7.33">Jer 7:33</reference> (note).
entries.content_plain: Verse 7 I will make void the counsel of Judah - Probably this refers to some determination made to proclaim themselves independent, and pay no more tribute to the Chaldeans. To be meat for the fowls - See on Jer 7:33 (note).

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen29788" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29789" type="x-p"/> I will cause them to eat the flesh of their sons - This was literally fulfilled when Jerusalem was besieged by the Romans. This also the prophet might have had in view.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen29789" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29790" type="x-p"/> Even so will I break this people and this city - The breaking of the bottle was the symbolical representation of the destruction of the city and of the state. <div eID="gen29790" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29791" type="x-p"/> That cannot be made whole again - This seems to refer rather to the final destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans, than to what was done by the Chaldeans. Jerusalem was healed after 70 years: but nearly 1800 years have elapsed since Jerusalem was taken and destroyed by the Romans; and it was then so broken, that it could not be made whole again.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen29793" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29794" type="x-p"/> Because they have hardened their necks - A metaphor taken from unruly and unbroken oxen, who resist the yoke, break and run away with their gears. So this people had broken and destroyed the yoke of the law.  <chapter eID="Jer.19"/> <div eID="gen29794" type="x-p"/>
